editorial.headline: The Systems That Keep Buildings Working Quietly
editorial.standfirst: A specialised installation activity for protective and performance systems, open to full foreign ownership nationally and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Some building work is designed to function quietly, but its scope is highly specific. This activity covers the installation of other building equipment and the installation, maintenance and repair of other equipment for civil buildings. The record gives concrete examples: lightning-protection systems; integrated vacuum systems; and insulation for heat, sound or vibration. That insulation includes acoustic covering panels, glass wool and rock wool. The code is defined by specialised systems placed into a built environment, with continuing maintenance and repair expressly included for the other civil-building equipment identified in its scope.

This is not a single-material category. A business can fall within the stated scope when its work concerns a lightning arrester, an integrated vacuum arrangement, or insulation that controls heat, sound or vibration. The examples matter because they describe installation work rather than leaving the activity as a generic construction label. They also show that the scope runs beyond fitting new equipment: it expressly reaches maintenance and repair for other civil-building equipment. The registration analysis should remain anchored to those listed systems and services.

At the national level, the activity is TERBUKA. It is available at every scale stated in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—and the national foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In practical terms, an undertaking carrying out the defined work may register at any of those four scales, while foreign ownership nationally may reach the full 100% ceiling. That position is attributed in the record to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. The national position supplied here is clear: the activity is open and the recorded ceiling permits complete foreign ownership.

Bali needs its own, narrower reading. The provincial moratorium blocks PMA registration for every Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI, island-wide and permanently. This activity, however, is not marked as blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns a Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi classification—Medium-High/High—which is why the record says the activity is not blocked by that moratorium. The honest conclusion is straightforward: the national 100% ceiling is the national ceiling, and Bali does not impose a moratorium block on this activity in the record. For a foreign investor, Bali is therefore available for PMA registration under this code rather than barred by the island-wide rule.
editorial.pullQuote: The national ceiling is 100%, and Bali does not place this activity behind its PMA moratorium.
